title: EmbeddingGemma 2: The Developer Guide to Multimodal Embeddings
summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 enables engineers to map text, images, and audio into a shared vector space for precise cross-modal retrieval in custom applications.
body_markdown:
## Connecting Gemini Embedding 2 to your existing workflows today


Integrating EmbeddingGemma 2 into your production pipeline transforms raw unstructured data into a standardized vector format that your automation tools can programmatically query. By establishing this connection, you eliminate the manual friction of data preparation. Your downstream models receive high-fidelity context without human intervention.


Reselling you a model is deciding your AI strategy for you. A privacy-first automation layer avoids this by running EmbeddingGemma 2 on your own provider key and infrastructure, ensuring model spend stays on your account at your direct rate.


By checking Bring-Your-Own-Key availability on the pricing page, architects can confirm that the automation layer does not dictate the model choice or markup the costs.


This keeps the strategy in your hands, accessible from any MCP client or AI chat, while processing 8,192-token documents at the true cost of the hardware.


### Option 1: The HTTP request integration for direct API calls


By bypassing the limitations of pre-built integrations, directly interfacing with the model via a standard web request gives the most granular control over payload parameters.


This method allows you to tune the embedding process specifically for retrieval, clustering, or classification tasks. The following steps outline the implementation:


1. Deploy Gemini Embedding 2 to a GPU provider like Hugging Face Inference Endpoints.
2. Create a new flow in your chosen automation environment.
3. Add an HTTP Request integration.
4. Set the Method to POST and the URL to your endpoint.


Once the connection is established, the output of this integration is the dynamic input for your vector database. Every new document added to your system is automatically indexed in real-time.


Every action configured in this way is immediately available as a tool for AI agents through a per-project MCP server.


By inspecting the Integrations Framework in the open source repository, developers can see how the same logic used for structured flows is exposed to agents in Claude or ChatGPT without a separate migration step.


This allows EmbeddingGemma 2 to function simultaneously as a background indexing step and a real-time retrieval tool for autonomous agents.


### Using OpenAI-compatible providers with Gemini Embedding 2


Many automation platforms include native "AI Provider" blocks that follow the OpenAI API specification.


You can repurpose these to call Gemini Embedding 2 by simply swapping the base URL. This approach allows teams to use existing, tested logic for error handling and retries while benefiting from the performance of Google’s open-weight embedding architecture.


By pointing these integrations to a local or private server running the model, you maintain data sovereignty without rewriting your entire automation logic.


### Running Gemini Embedding 2 locally with MCP servers


Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers act as a standardized bridge between your local hardware and your automation tools. You can run EmbeddingGemma 2 on-premises while keeping it accessible to cloud-based flows. This configuration is essential for organizations with strict data residency requirements.


**Sensitive information is processed locally before only the anonymized vector embeddings are sent to the cloud.** Deploying via MCP ensures that your automation environment can scale its resource usage based on the specific hardware available in your private stack.
